answer_raw:
Your carry-on limits depend heavily on your fare class, with size dimensions generally hovering around **55 × 35 × 25 cm**.

**LATAM** — The main cabin bag limit is **55 × 35 × 25 cm** with a max weight of **12 kg** as of August 2026 [5]. Note that the **35 cm** side is a common point of failure for bag compliance [3]; also, the **Basic** fare only includes a personal item, so you must purchase at least a **Light** fare to bring a cabin bag [5].

**GOL** — One handbag/backpack up to **10 kg** and one small suitcase ups to **10 kg** (max **55 × 35 × 25 cm**) are allowed as carry-on baggage, undated [8].

**Azul** — One main bag up to **55 × 35 × 25 cm** and **10 kg**, plus one underseat personal item up to **45 × 35 × 20 cm** is allowed as of June 2026 [1][3].

**Packing Strategy**
For a three-week trip, focus on versatile layers and compression to stay within the **8–10 kg** limits common in the region [4].

*   **Clothing**: Pack wrinkle-resistant fabrics and one "smart-casual" outfit for city hubs like São Paulo [3]. Focus on layers to handle temperature shifts between high-altitude Andes and coastal cities [2].
*   **Footlet/Footwear**: One pair of sturdy walking shoes worn on the plane, plus one pair of sandals or lighter shoes packed.
*   **Tech/Essentials**: A high-capacity power bank, universal adapters, and a dedicated small pouch for liquids (max 100 ml per container) [1].
*   **Organization**: Use compression packing cubes to manage volume and keep weight distributed for easier maneuvering through check-in-only gates [4].
